REQUIREMENTS FOR ORTHOPAEDIC IMPLANTS 

PART 11 ULTRA-HIGH MOLECULAR WEIGHT POLYETHYLENE, MOULDED FORM 

( ISO Title : Implants for Surgery — Ultra-High Molecular 
Weight Polyethylene — Part 2 : Moulded Forms ) 



National Foreword 

This Indian Standard ( Part 11 ), which is identical with ISO 5834/2-1985 'Implants for 
surgery — Ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene — Part 2 : Moulded forms' issued by the 
International Organization for Standardization (ISO), was adopted by the Bureau of Indian 
Standards on the recommendations of the Orthopaedic Instruments and Accessories Sectional 
Committee and approval of the Consumer Products and Medical Instruments Division Council. 

in the adopted standard, certain terminology and conventions are not identical with those used 
in Indian Standards; attention is particularly drawn to the following: 

Comma ( , ) has been used as a decimal marker while in Indian Standards the current 
practice is to use a point ( - ) 3S the decimal marker. 

Wherever the words international Standard' appear, referring to this standard, they should 
be read as 'Indian Standard'. 



Adopted 13 November 1987

IS: 6347 (Part 11 ) - 1987 
ISO 5834/2-1985 



1 Scope and field of application 

This part of ISO 5834 specifies the requirements and cor- 
responding test methods for moulded forms made from ultra- 
high molecular weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) for use in the 
manufacture of surgical implants. 

It does not apply to finished products. 



4 Material 

The moulded forms shall be made from either Type A or 
Type B UHMWPE powder complying with the requirements of 
ISO 5834/1. 



5 Manufacturing requirements 



2 References 

ISO 179, Plastics — Determination of Charpy impact strength 
of rigid materials. 

ISO 527, Plastics — Determination of tensile properties. '^^ 

ISO/R 1183, Plastics — Methods for determining the density 
and relative density (specific gravity) of plastics excluding 
cellular plastics, 

ISO 3451/1, Plastics — Determination of ash — Parti : 
General methods. 

ISO 5834/1, Implants for surgery — Ultra-high molecular 
weight polyethylene — Part 1 : Powder form, 2) 



3 Classification 

The material shall be classified as follows : 
Type 1 — Compression moulded material. 
Type 2 — Extruded material. 



5.1 The moulded material supplied for each order shall be 
identified by batch or lot numbers. 

NOTE — "Batch" or "lot" refers to moulded forms for which testing 
has been carried out and for which discrete records are kept. 

5.2 The material shall be subjected by the manufacturer to a 
stress-relief annealing process. 

NOTE — Subsequent transit and storage may re-tntroduce stresses 
that should be relieved by the manufacturer of a finished implant. 



6 Properties 

6.1 Test requirements 

The test requirements for moulded forms shall be as given in 
the table. 

6.2 Particulate matter 

In an area 400 mm x 800 mm of the moulded material not 
more than 10 particles shall be visible on the surface upon in-

7.5 Tensile stress at break 

Tensile stress at break crp shall be measured during the test 
described in 7.4. 



7 Methods of test 



7.1 Test conditions 



Unless otherwise specified, the testing specified in 7.2 to 7.7 
shall be conducted under standard conditions of 23 ± 2 °C 
and 50 ± 5 % relative humidity after storage of the test 
specimens for at least 16 h under these conditions. 



7.2 Density 

The density shall be measured by means of method A (buoy- 
ancy procedure) specified in ISC/R 1183 using at least three 
specimens. 



7.3 Ash content 

The ash content shall be determined in accordance with 
ISO 3451/1, performing duplicate tests on each of two test 
specimens. 



7.6 Elongation at break 

Elongation at break shall be measured during the test described 
in 7.4, 



7.7 IMotched impact strength (Charpy) 

The notched impact strength a^ shall be determined by the im- 
pact test specified in ISO 179 using at least five standard test 
specimens, type 3, a sharp notch at an angle of 15° and a depth 
of 3,4 mm. 



8 Identification marking 

Each item supplied shall be identified with arx impressed batch 
or lot number and marked with the letter M. 

NOTE — The marking, which may also be a serial number,, with 
reference to the batch or lot number, may be repeated at intervals 
along the length of the item. 



7.4 Tensile stress at yield 

The tensile stress at yield o^ shall be determined by the tensile 
test specified in ISO 527 on at least five test specimens of 
thickness 1,5 mm at test temperatures of 23 °C and 120 °C 
using test speed F{100mm/min ± 10%) and 
D (25 mm/min ± 10 %) respectively. 



9 Test certificate 

The supplier shall furnish with each delivery a test certificate 
signed by a duly authorized representative of the supplier 
stating conformance with the requirements of this International 
Standard. In this certificate the results of the tests conducted 



IS: 5347 (Part 11 ) - 1987 
ISO 5834/2-1985 



shall be stated. The test certificate shall include the following 
information : 

a) purchase order number; 

b) the number of this International Standard (ISO 5834/2); 

c) batch or lot number or serial number with reference to 
the batch or lot number; 

d) number of items; 

e} test values according to the relevant clauses of this 
International Standard; 

f) dateis) of test. 



10 Labelling 

The external packaging of the supplied moulded forms shall be 
marked with the following information : 

a) batch or lot number or serial number with reference to 
the batch or lot number; 

b) mass of materials; 

c) manufacturer's name or trademark; 

d) purchase order number; 

e) the number of this International Standard {ISO 5834/2). 



Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, India
